- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses bottoming or toping; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 14-day moving average as anchor for correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model tends to drift; apply smoothing filter or use 7-day average to dampen noise.
